question: What does the thermic effect of food (TEF) refer to?

options.A: The heat lost through the skin during a fever
options.B: The calories burned during cardiovascular exercise
options.C: The basal energy used by the liver during sleep
options.D: The energy used to process and digest nutrients

explanation: Your body actually burns calories just chewing, digesting, and processing food. That's what we call TEF!

question: What is a major error a nurse can make during community mobilisation?

options.A: Asking local leaders for permission to enter the village
options.B: Taking over leadership and making decisions for the community
options.C: Teaching mothers how to prepare oral rehydration salt
options.D: Working with local volunteers to clean up the environment

explanation: Nurses should facilitate and empower, not take control and rob the community of their self-reliance. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is the body's main way of stopping hormone levels from climbing too high?

options.A: Enzymatic destruction
options.B: Receptor downregulation
options.C: Positive feedback
options.D: Negative feedback

explanation: Negative feedback is like a thermostat: when hormone levels get too high, a signal is sent to slow down production and bring things back to normal.

question: Which concept forms the core foundation of a clean delivery kit?

options.A: The six cleans of childbirth
options.B: Immediate surgical intervention
options.C: Routine administration of heavy IV antibiotics
options.D: Continuous electronic fetal monitoring

explanation: The kit is built directly around ensuring hands, surfaces, perineum, cord tools, cord ties, and baby wraps are completely clean. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h1)

question: What is a common social double standard regarding the sexuality of adolescent boys and girls?

options.A: Girls are labeled immoral for sexual activity while boys are praised
options.B: Schools teach boys exclusively about menstruation and hygiene
options.C: Society expects girls to be sexually aggressive and dominant
options.D: Boys are denied clinic access while girls receive free medications

explanation: Sad but true—society often judges girls harshly for exploring their sexuality while treating the exact same behavior in boys as just a normal phase.

question: Which assessment is most important to keep checking for a patient in an oxygen tent?

options.A: Respiratory rate and work of breathing
options.B: Bowel sounds and abdominal circumference
options.C: Daily weight and fluid intake volume
options.D: Neurological reflex response scores

explanation: Since oxygen tents treat breathing problems, always keep a close eye on how hard the child is working to breathe and their breathing rate.

question: Why do medications absorb so slowly when given as an intradermal injection?

options.A: The body attacks the drug before it can dissolve
options.B: The dermal layer has a very limited blood supply
options.C: The needle gauge is too small to release much fluid
options.D: The outer layer of skin blocks fluid movement

explanation: You've got this! The dermis doesn't have as many blood vessels as other layers, which is actually a good thing—it keeps the medication right where we put it for tests like Mantoux.

question: Why is building an early, trusting relationship with an expectant mother so important for a nurse?

options.A: It ensures the mother will have a completely pain-free labor
options.B: It encourages the mother to return for subsequent clinic visits
options.C: It completely eliminates all risks of genetic disorders in the fetus
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory tests during pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! When mothers trust us, they feel safe and are much more likely to keep coming back for their clinic check-ups, keeping both mum and baby safe.

question: Why is a nurse's daily report on how much a patient ate so helpful to the dietitian?

options.A: It allows the nurse to prescribe new therapeutic diets alone
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory blood test investigations
options.C: It helps the dietitian evaluate if nutritional targets are met
options.D: It determines the daily work schedule of the kitchen staff

explanation: Exactly! Nurses are at the bedside every day, so tracking actual meal intake helps the whole team know if the patient is getting enough nourishment.

question: What happens if a nursing unit allows its stock levels to fall below the minimum safety threshold?

options.A: The storage room becomes much cleaner and easier to clean
options.B: The hospital pharmacy saves a lot of money on bulk purchases
options.C: Expired items automatically get removed from the shelves
options.D: Patients may face dangerous delays in treatment due to shortages

explanation: Falling below minimum safety stock means the ward risks running out of crucial supplies during an emergency. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h4)

question: What exactly is a community health risk?

options.A: The total cost of running a primary health care clinic
options.B: Any factor increasing the chance of illness or injury for a group
options.C: A personal medical diagnosis given inside a hospital ward
options.D: A genetic disease passed down through generations in a family

explanation: Think of community health risks as collective dangers that affect many people together, rather than just one person's isolated sickness. You've got this!

question: What are the standard settings for a hospital autoclave?

options.A: 72 degrees Celsius for 15 seconds
options.B: 100 degrees Celsius at atmospheric pressure
options.C: 160 degrees Celsius with dry heat
options.D: 121 degrees Celsius at 15 psi

explanation: Remember 121 degrees Celsius and 15 pounds of pressure! That magic combo of hot steam kills spores reliably every time.

question: What does the term 'aging in place' mean for elderly patients?

options.A: Traveling across the country without any medical help
options.B: Staying in the emergency room for extended observation
options.C: Living safely in one's own home rather than a facility
options.D: Moving into a large hospital permanently

explanation: Aging in place refers to older adults remaining in their private residences while receiving needed support services. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h4)

question: How do cultural expectations in Nigeria often worsen the emotional strain of male infertility?

options.A: Society places heavy emphasis on fatherhood and family lineage, leading to deep personal stigma
options.B: Cultural practices strictly forbid men from undergoing any form of medical testing
options.C: Traditional healers are legally required to manage all reproductive health conditions
options.D: Communities automatically blame the female partner, protecting the man from stress

explanation: The strong cultural expectation to bear children creates intense psychological pressure and shame when fertility challenges arise. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: Why do they sometimes give patients gas-producing crystals along with the barium?

options.A: To numb the throat during swallowing
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling nauseated by the barium
options.C: To speed up the emptying of the stomach contents
options.D: To provide a double-contrast view of the stomach lining

explanation: Brilliant! The gas blows the stomach open like a balloon, pressing the barium against the walls so we get super-clear pictures. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why do we need multiple organizations teaming up to prevent unsafe abortions?

options.A: No single healthcare facility has the resources to handle all community reproductive needs alone
options.B: Government policies require every clinic to report pregnancy tests to the police
options.C: Hospitals are legally prohibited from providing contraceptive counseling directly to teenagers
options.D: Community groups refuse to work with doctors unless funded by international donors

explanation: Exactly! Tackling big public health issues means sharing resources, ideas, and reach across different groups so no one clinic has to carry the whole load.

question: Why do we prefer a closed bladder irrigation system over an open one?

options.A: It allows the nurse to bypass the need for a physician order
options.B: It lowers the risk of introducing bacteria into the bladder
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling any bladder spasms at all
options.D: It requires much less total fluid volume over twenty-four hours

explanation: Keeping everything connected means fewer germs can slip inside, which helps your patient avoid a nasty UTI.

question: Why do conditions that stop bile salt production lead to a shortage of fat-soluble vitamins?

options.A: Vitamins require acidic bile to transform into water-soluble molecules
options.B: Without bile, the stomach cannot produce enough intrinsic factor for vitamin uptake
options.C: Bile salts act as direct chemical carriers for vitamins A, D, E, and K in the blood
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins depend on lipid micelles for transport across the brush border

explanation: Spot on! Vitamins A, D, E, and K love fat, so they need bile to form tiny packages called micelles that ferry them close enough to the gut wall to be absorbed.

question: What is the appropriate action for a general nurse when a patient requires highly specialized medical nutrition therapy for a rare metabolic disease?

options.A: Refer the patient to a registered dietitian or specialist
options.B: Ignore the condition since nutrition is not a nursing concern
options.C: Guess the correct nutrient formula and prescribe it immediately
options.D: Discharge the patient to avoid having to deal with the complexity

explanation: Nurses must recognize their scope of practice and collaborate by referring complex cases to experts like dietitians. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h4)

question: Why did Nigerian health planners eventually shift their focus toward rural communities?

options.A: Rural areas had no traditional healers left
options.B: Urban residents refused to visit government hospitals
options.C: The majority of the population lived in rural areas with limited medical access
options.D: Colonial laws prohibited urban healthcare expansion

explanation: That makes total sense—since most people lived outside the cities without clinics nearby, health services had to reach out to the grassroots.

question: What does a genetic predisposition to a mental disorder mean?

options.A: The person will definitely develop the illness as they age
options.B: The illness cannot be treated with modern psychiatric medications
options.C: The condition was caused entirely by a poor diet in childhood
options.D: The person has a higher chance of developing the condition

explanation: Genetic predisposition means a person carries inherited vulnerabilities that make them more likely to develop a disorder if other triggers are present. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient with Type AB blood needs an emergency red blood cell transfusion. Why are they called universal red cell recipients?

options.A: Their red blood cells contain no surface antigens
options.B: Their body rapidly destroys all incoming donor antibodies
options.C: Their immune system is completely inactive during stress
options.D: Their plasma lacks both anti-A and anti-B antibodies

explanation: Because Type AB plasma does not contain anti-A or anti-B antibodies, it will not attack incoming red blood cells from other ABO groups. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h2)

question: What technology does an autoclave use to sterilize infectious medical waste?

options.A: Ultraviolet radiation
options.B: Pressurized steam
options.C: Open-air sun drying
options.D: Chemical bleach spray

explanation: Correct! Autoclaves use high heat and pressure to kill all germs on medical equipment.

question: What is the main job of a patient referral form in community health?

options.A: To replace the patient's daily hospital bed ticket
options.B: To serve as a permanent financial receipt for clinic services
options.C: To connect a patient with higher levels of specialized care
options.D: To discharge a patient permanently from all medical follow-up

explanation: You've got this! Referral forms act like a bridge, safely moving a patient from our basic community clinics up to advanced centers when they need extra specialist attention.

question: What is the most common type of primary heart tumour found in adults?

options.A: Papillary fibroelastoma
options.B: Rhabdomyoma
options.C: Myxoma
options.D: Angiosarcoma

explanation: Myxomas take the crown here! They are the most common primary heart tumours in adults and usually like to set up shop in the left atrium. Keep up the great memorisation!

question: What happens to liquid vaccines containing aluminum if they accidentally freeze in the vaccine fridge?

options.A: The vaccine becomes more concentrated and requires dilution before use
options.B: The vaccine transforms into a live-attenuated strain
options.C: Freezing has no negative effect as long as the vial is thawed before injection
options.D: The adjuvant structure breaks down, permanently destroying vaccine potency

explanation: Freezing ruins the special aluminum particles that help trigger the immune response. Once frozen, they can't be saved—always check that cold chain!

question: What is the biggest risk you watch out for at skeletal traction pin sites?

options.A: Development of bone infection like osteomyelitis
options.B: Rapid healing that fuses the pin to the bed sheets
options.C: Complete numbness of the entire unaffected leg
options.D: Permanent discoloration of the surrounding skin

explanation: Spot on! Because the pins go right through the skin, bacteria can travel down the metal and cause a serious bone infection. Good thing nurses keep a close eye on this!

question: A mother in labor suddenly starts having severe seizures from pre-eclampsia at a rural clinic. Which emergency drug should you give?

options.A: Magnesium sulfate
options.B: Routine prenatal vitamins
options.C: Injectable iron sucrose
options.D: Normal saline tablets

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the gold-standard emergency medication for stopping and preventing dangerous eclamptic seizures.

question: What is the main difference between an IDP and a refugee?

options.A: Refugees do not need humanitarian aid
options.B: IDPs have crossed an international border
options.C: Refugees receive free housing from the United Nations
options.D: IDPs stay inside their own country's borders

explanation: Think of it this way: IDPs (Internally Displaced Persons) move within their own country, while refugees cross an international border to find safety.

question: What is the main difference between physical dependence on a drug and psychological addiction?

options.A: Addiction stops the moment you lower the dose
options.B: Dependence only happens to people who abuse drugs
options.C: Dependence is a normal body adaptation, while addiction involves strong cravings
options.D: Dependence stops future pain relief from working

explanation: Physical dependence just means your body gets used to a medicine and reacts if you stop too fast. Addiction is a brain disease marked by compulsive cravings and loss of control.

question: A patient with a known femur tumor suddenly cries out in severe pain after rolling over in bed and can no longer bear weight. What likely happened?

options.A: A normal muscle cramp
options.B: A pathological fracture
options.C: Deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Acute joint dislocation

explanation: Because the tumor weakens the bone structure, even a tiny movement like rolling over can cause it to break. This is called a pathological fracture!

question: A patient on clofazimine panics because their skin is turning a dark brownish-red. What should you tell them?

options.A: Scrub the discolored skin vigorously with medicated soap during daily hygiene routines.
options.B: Explain that this is a common, harmless side effect that will gradually fade after treatment stops.
options.C: Report an emergency adverse drug reaction to the primary prescriber for medication substitution.
options.D: Advise the patient to stop taking all multidrug therapy medications immediately.

explanation: You got it! Clofazimine is known for changing skin color, but it's completely safe and temporary. Reassuring the patient goes a long way!

question: What makes adaptive immunity different from innate immunity?

options.A: It relies entirely on physical skin barriers to block infections
options.B: It only functions during the first year of a human life
options.C: It creates specific immunological memory against targeted pathogens
options.D: It responds instantly without recognizing specific antigens

explanation: Adaptive immunity tailors its response to specific antigens and remembers them for a faster defense during future exposures. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in a remote village has severe bleeding, but her family wastes two hours trying traditional herbs before looking for transport. Which delay has occurred?

options.A: Delay in reaching care
options.B: Delay in deciding to seek care
options.C: Delay in post-delivery recovery
options.D: Delay in receiving care

explanation: Waiting to seek help because of trying home remedies or not understanding the urgency represents the first delay in the model. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h3)

question: What usually happens when the government health sector and voluntary agencies fail to communicate well?

options.A: Complete elimination of poverty in rural areas
options.B: Immediate reduction in community disease rates
options.C: Instant eradication of all infectious diseases
options.D: Duplication of health efforts and wasted resources

explanation: Well reasoned! Without good teamwork, two agencies might end up doing the exact same thing in one village while leaving another village completely ignored.

question: What makes an abortion procedure classified as "unsafe"?

options.A: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally during the first trimester
options.B: A legal termination performed in a fully equipped hospital
options.C: A procedure done by unskilled persons or in poor medical environments
options.D: Any abortion that requires the use of surgical instruments

explanation: You've got this! An abortion is unsafe if it's carried out by people without proper training or in places that lack basic medical standards. Keeping patients safe means knowing the difference.

question: What is the main job of a research codebook?

options.A: To lock up physical research files in a metal cabinet
options.B: To list the personal home addresses of study participants
options.C: To explain what each numerical code stands for in the study
options.D: To record the daily vital signs of hospital patients

explanation: Think of a codebook as your translation key. It reminds you what specific numbers (like 1 for Male and 2 for Female) actually represent.

question: Why is it important for nurses to talk and debrief with colleagues after a patient's traumatic death?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any personal sleep or rest
options.B: It helps process difficult emotions and prevents burnout
options.C: It ensures the family receives accurate medical bills
options.D: It is required to update hospital accreditation charts

explanation: You got it! Debriefing gives you a safe space to unload heavy emotions so you can protect your own mental health and prevent burnout.

question: Why is it important for nurses to ask direct questions about hopelessness to clients with chronic illness?

options.A: To uncover hidden thoughts of depression or self-harm early
options.B: To make the client stop talking about their physical pain
options.C: To prove to the doctor that the client has a psychiatric disorder
options.D: To fill out the hospital admission paperwork faster

explanation: Directly asking about emotional pain allows nurses to protect vulnerable clients and provide timely mental health support. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the correct way to store an epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: Leave it inside a parked car during hot sunny days for easy access.
options.B: Store it tightly sealed inside the kitchen refrigerator to preserve potency.
options.C: Wrap it in thick cotton padding to protect it from accidental freezing.
options.D: Keep it at room temperature and protect it from extreme heat and light.

explanation: Correct! Epinephrine loses its potency quickly when exposed to direct sunlight or heat, so keeping it safe at room temp ensures it works when an emergency strikes.

question: Why do modern hospitals emphasize respectful maternity care?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any medical issues
options.B: It reduces the cost of building new maternity wards
options.C: It encourages women to choose facility delivery instead of staying home
options.D: It replaces the need for any medications during labor

explanation: Nobody wants to visit a harsh nurse! When women feel welcomed and valued in the clinic, they are happy to come back for safe deliveries.

question: An elderly patient has thinning skin and less fat under the skin. What is the most important nursing care?

options.A: Applying heavy makeup to cover up skin discoloration
options.B: Encouraging vigorous daily scrubbing during baths
options.C: Restricting fluid intake to keep the skin dry
options.D: Turning the patient regularly to prevent pressure sores

explanation: Brilliant! Without that cushioning layer of fat, older patients easily develop pressure sores, so helping them change positions regularly is key to keeping their skin safe.

question: What is a major feature that sets connective tissue apart from epithelial tissue?

options.A: Its cells are always tightly packed together without space
options.B: It never has any blood supply running through it
options.C: It contains a large amount of extracellular matrix
options.D: It is found exclusively on the outer surface of the skin

explanation: Unlike epithelial cells which pack tightly together, connective tissue cells are spread out in a rich matrix of fibers and ground substance.

question: Why should nurses rotate injection sites for patients who need frequent medications?

options.A: It ensures the medication reaches the bloodstream much faster
options.B: It stops bacteria from multiplying on the surface of the skin
options.C: It gives previous tissue time to heal instead of forming hard scar tissue
options.D: It prevents the needle from becoming dull during the procedure

explanation: Sticking the exact same spot over and over causes fibrous scar knots, which hurt the patient and make drug absorption difficult. Rotating sites keeps tissue healthy!

question: Who produces the majority of domestic food supply in Nigeria?

options.A: Importing syndicates
options.B: Multinational corporations
options.C: Smallholder farmers
options.D: State-owned plantations

explanation: Small-scale local farmers do most of the primary growing and harvesting that feeds the nation. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h2)

question: A patient is recovering from a stroke and needs help with walking and swallowing. Who should be on this care team?

options.A: The pharmacist and the hospital security personnel only
options.B: Only the patient's family members making independent choices
options.C: The nurse, physiotherapist, speech therapist, and the patient
options.D: Only the attending physician and the hospital accountant

explanation: Exactly! Recovery takes a village—different specialists are needed to tackle different physical challenges alongside the patient.

question: Why should healthcare workers partner with traditional birth attendants (TBAs) instead of chasing them away?

options.A: To replace trained midwives with TBAs
options.B: To encourage them to refer pregnant women to clinics for skilled care
options.C: To let them manage severe bleeding at home
options.D: To train them to perform major village surgeries

explanation: Well reasoned! Since many rural women trust TBAs, working with them helps bridge the gap and guides mothers safely to professional clinic care.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical long-term complication of untreated lung flukes?

options.A: Recurrent pneumothorax
options.B: Bronchiectasis
options.C: Glomerular kidney failure
options.D: Pulmonary fibrosis

explanation: You got it! Kidney failure isn't a direct result of lung flukes, but the others are classic respiratory complications when the lungs take chronic damage.

question: If an intracardiac needle is placed too far to the side (laterally), which major organ might accidentally get punctured?

options.A: The kidneys
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The lungs
options.D: The stomach

explanation: Great thinking! Because the lungs sit right next to the heart, pushing a needle too far sideways risks puncturing lung tissue and causing a collapse.

question: What two extra services make a CEmOC facility different from a BEmOC facility?

options.A: Manual vacuum aspiration and neonatal bag-valve-mask ventilation
options.B: Administration of intravenous antibiotics and magnesium sulfate
options.C: Blood transfusion and emergency Caesarean section surgery
options.D: Routine antenatal ultrasound and postpartum family planning

explanation: While BEmOC covers seven basic functions, Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmOC) steps it up with blood transfusions and major surgeries like C-sections.

question: What main effect does digoxin have on the heart?

options.A: It speeds up electrical conduction through all nodes
options.B: It removes excess body water through the kidneys
options.C: It relaxes the coronary arteries to increase blood flow
options.D: It increases contraction force and slows heart rate

explanation: Digoxin is fascinating! It acts like a double agent: it makes each squeeze stronger, but slows down the overall heart rate so the heart can rest and fill properly.

question: What is the medical term for the exaggerated inward curve of the lower back seen in pregnancy?

options.A: Cervical subluxation
options.B: Compensatory lumbar lordosis
options.C: Thoracic scoliosis
options.D: Lateral kyphosis

explanation: Lordosis is just the natural inward curve of the lower back. During pregnancy, it becomes more pronounced (exaggerated) to help balance out the heavy bump.

question: Which of the following is included in a comprehensive nutrition history?

options.A: Family tree and genetic ancestry
options.B: Medical history and medication use
options.C: Recent travel history outside the country
options.D: Workplace safety hazard inspections

explanation: Medical conditions and medications heavily influence how the body absorbs and uses nutrients, making them essential parts of a nutrition history. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h3)

question: Where do the first nerve fibers (preganglionic neurons) of the sympathetic nervous system start?

options.A: Thoracic and lumbar regions of the spinal cord
options.B: Cervical region of the spinal cord exclusively
options.C: Directly inside the wall of target organs
options.D: Brainstem and sacral spinal cord

explanation: You can remember sympathetic outflow easily by its location: it arises from the chest (thoracic) and lower back (lumbar) areas of the spine, which is why it's called thoracolumbar.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal emotional challenge many women face during pregnancy?

options.A: Mood swings driven by profound hormonal shifts
options.B: Heightened anxiety about the upcoming labor process
options.C: Stress regarding financial changes and parenting duties
options.D: Complete emotional numbness and lack of heartbeat awareness

explanation: Well spotted! Mood swings, stress, and anxiety are totally normal with pregnancy hormones, but complete emotional numbness is not a typical response.

question: What is the main job of the Bartholin's glands?

options.A: To secrete mucus for lubrication
options.B: To produce the female egg cells
options.C: To maintain acidic vaginal pH
options.D: To filter waste from the blood

explanation: Correct! These glands release fluid to keep the vaginal opening lubricated.

question: What physical sign involves a bluish color of the skin due to low oxygen in the blood?

options.A: Jaundice
options.B: Pallor
options.C: Cyanosis
options.D: Erythema

explanation: Cyanosis is the bluish tint seen on the skin and lips when deoxygenated hemoglobin levels rise. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h5)

question: What is a major risk of overfeeding a critically ill patient on a ventilator?

options.A: Extra carbon dioxide production making it harder to breathe off the ventilator
options.B: Total elimination of the need for IV fluids
options.C: Rapid healing of surgical wounds
options.D: A sudden drop in blood sugar levels

explanation: Giving too many calories—especially from carbs—makes the body produce extra carbon dioxide. This makes breathing much harder for a patient trying to come off a ventilator!

question: When does the first stage of labour officially come to an end?

options.A: When regular uterine contractions first begin
options.B: When the baby's head emerges from the vagina
options.C: When the placenta is successfully delivered
options.D: When the cervix is fully dilated at 10 centimeters

explanation: Stage one is all about opening the cervix. Once it hits 10 cm, that stage is wrapped up and it's time to push!

question: Why can't we use very heavy weights with skin traction?

options.A: Heavy weights will damage the skin and slip off
options.B: Skin traction requires a surgical operating room
options.C: Heavy weights make the patient fall asleep faster
options.D: Skin bones cannot support heavy metal devices

explanation: Skin is tough, but it's not made to carry heavy loads! Too much weight will cause blisters, tears, or just slip right out of the straps.

question: A client comes to you asking for advice on diet and irregular ovulation. What is the best starting point?

options.A: Focus on whole foods, healthy weight management, and essential micronutrients
options.B: Rely entirely on heavy vitamin supplements instead of eating meals
options.C: Drink large amounts of caffeinated coffee to boost resting metabolism
options.D: Eliminate all carbohydrates completely from your daily meals

explanation: Awesome choice! Real, wholesome food and steady weight management give the body the stable foundation it needs for natural hormonal balance.

question: Why is it so tricky to spot an asymptomatic carrier during a disease outbreak?

options.A: Pathogens cannot be detected in their bodily fluids
options.B: They show no outward signs of illness but can still spread the pathogen to others
options.C: Their laboratory blood tests always return completely normal results
options.D: They refuse to answer questions about their daily activities

explanation: That's why outbreaks can be sneaky. These carriers feel completely fine and show zero symptoms, yet they can still pass the germs along to others without knowing it.

question: Why is it important to ask about past surgical complications, such as a bad reaction to anesthesia?

options.A: To calculate the exact hospital bill in advance
options.B: To check if the patient has valid health insurance
options.C: To prevent similar dangerous reactions during future procedures
options.D: To determine what food the patient likes to eat

explanation: Knowing about previous adverse anesthesia reactions allows the surgical and anesthesia team to take safety precautions. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why are certain medications supplied to the hospital ward in powdered form instead of ready-to-use liquids?

options.A: Powders do not require any mathematical calculations to mix
options.B: Powders have a much longer shelf-life before reconstitution
options.C: Powders can be swallowed directly if the injection fails
options.D: Powders automatically dissolve in normal room air moisture

explanation: Many active drug compounds break down quickly in liquid form. Manufacturers supply them as powders to maintain stability until right before use. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h1)

question: Which personal trait helps a nurse leader bounce back quickly from tough ward stresses?

options.A: Compliance
options.B: Rigidity
options.C: Resilience
options.D: Aloofness

explanation: Resilience is your inner strength. It's what helps you keep your cool and bounce back after dealing with a really difficult shift or unexpected workplace stress.

question: What is the main goal of using the Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) cycle in healthcare?

options.A: To punish nurses who fail to follow hospital guidelines
options.B: To test and evaluate small changes for quality improvement
options.C: To calculate monthly nursing staff salaries and overtime
options.D: To diagnose complex infectious diseases in emergency rooms

explanation: The PDSA cycle gives us a simple, step-by-step way to test small improvements and see if they actually work before rolling them out everywhere.

question: Which vitamin supplement is routinely given to pregnant mothers to prevent neural tube defects?

options.A: Folic acid
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Iron

explanation: Spot on! Folic acid is vital for early cell division and helps prevent serious birth defects of the brain and spine.

question: During a pelvic exam, what physical sign would you expect in a patient with Type II FGM?

options.A: A completely sealed vaginal opening with a tiny pinhole
options.B: An intact hymen with no external scars
options.C: Extensive scar tissue and absence of the labia minora
options.D: Enlarged, hypertrophied Bartholin glands

explanation: Well done! The removal of both the clitoris and labia minora leaves clear signs of scar tissue and missing external structures.

question: What is the main advantage of Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT)?

options.A: Making the medication taste significantly sweeter for children
options.B: Eliminating the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: Preventing drug resistance and clearing remaining parasites
options.D: Allowing the entire treatment course to last only one hour

explanation: Spot on! Combining a fast-acting drug with a partner drug clears the malaria completely and stops resistant strains from developing.

question: What does a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM) tell you?

options.A: The exact number of doses remaining inside the glass vial
options.B: Whether heat exposure has damaged the vaccine's potency
options.C: Whether the vaccine container has been contaminated with bacteria
options.D: The precise manufacturing date printed on the cardboard box

explanation: Think of the VVM as a heat-watchdog! It changes color when exposed to too much heat, letting you know if the vaccine is still safe to use.

question: In the Nutrition Care Process, what does the letter 'P' stand for in a PES statement?

options.A: Patient
options.B: Prevention
options.C: Protocol
options.D: Problem

explanation: You're crushing it! PES stands for Problem, Etiology, and Signs/Symptoms, helping us clearly pinpoint the patient's nutritional issue.

question: Why is it helpful to raise the head of the bed slightly when sliding a bedpan under a patient?

options.A: It stops bad room odors
options.B: It keeps the bedpan from slipping
options.C: It mimics a natural sitting posture
options.D: It stops them from falling asleep

explanation: You're right! Gravity is our friend—a slight lift helps the patient pass waste naturally and comfortably.

question: Why is collaboration with traditional and religious leaders important in community mental health care?

options.A: They replace the need for professional nurses and social workers entirely
options.B: They provide the financial funding for all federal hospital budgets
options.C: They hold significant influence and can help mobilize the community against stigma
options.D: They are legally required to write official psychiatric prescriptions

explanation: Because many community members trust local and religious leaders, their involvement helps change negative attitudes and encourages families to seek help early. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h4)

question: Why can a man still cause a pregnancy right after getting a vasectomy?

options.A: Seminal fluid still requires three months to regenerate its chemistry
options.B: The body continues to produce live sperm inside the vas deferens tubes
options.C: Sperm already stored above the surgical cut remain active for weeks
options.D: The surgical incisions take several weeks to close completely

explanation: You nailed it! There is still a leftover supply of sperm stored further up that needs to be cleared out through ejaculation.

question: Why do community health nurses keep a close eye on people living in the same house as a leprosy patient?

options.A: They are forced to pay for the patient's hospital bills
options.B: They are at higher risk because they spend so much time together
options.C: They are legally banned from leaving the house during treatment
options.D: They must swallow preventive antibiotics for years

explanation: Living closely under one roof means more exposure time, so checking family members regularly helps catch any early signs. Fantastic job completing this set!

question: What should you do when a clear-headed home care patient refuses a necessary treatment?

options.A: Ask family members to pressure the patient into agreeing
options.B: Educate on the risks, respect the choice, and document the refusal
options.C: Immediately discharge the patient from the home care agency
options.D: Administer the treatment anyway to prevent complications

explanation: Well done! Always give them the facts so they understand the risks, but remember: competent adults have the final say over their own bodies.

question: What do we call the lifelong process of learning what society expects from males and females?

options.A: The legal right to vote regardless of a person's gender identity
options.B: The lifelong process of learning society's expectations for males and females
options.C: A medical procedure used to alter a person's biological sex characteristics
options.D: A hospital policy ensuring equal pay for male and female nurses

explanation: From childhood, family and society teach us how we are 'supposed' to act, dress, and behave based on our gender. That learning process is gender socialization!

question: What makes interpersonal communication (IPC) the most effective channel for achieving behaviour change?

options.A: It relies entirely on written pamphlets rather than spoken words.
options.B: It allows for direct interaction, immediate feedback, and trust-building.
options.C: It can reach millions of people across the entire country instantly.
options.D: It requires no special training or preparation from the nurse.

explanation: Face-to-face communication lets nurses answer specific questions and build personal trust, which drives behavior change. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why does severe anaemia put a mother at high risk for heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage)?

options.A: The placenta remains permanently attached to the uterine wall
options.B: The exhausted uterine muscle fails to contract effectively after delivery
options.C: Low red blood cells cause high blood pressure in the arteries
options.D: Blood clotting factors are completely absent in all pregnant women

explanation: Think of it this way: muscles need oxygen to work hard. When blood is low on oxygen-carrying red cells, the uterus gets tired and can't clamp down tightly after birth to shut off the bleeding vessels.

question: A client is charting her basal body temperature (BBT). What is the key thing she must know about this method?

options.A: It prevents pregnancy by killing sperm in the uterus.
options.B: It measures hormone levels inside her bloodstream directly.
options.C: It confirms that ovulation has already taken place.
options.D: It predicts the exact hour ovulation will happen today.

explanation: Because the slight temperature jump is driven by progesterone *after* release, BBT charting is great for confirming ovulation happened, rather than predicting it ahead of time.

question: What step immediately follows the physician writing a prescription in the unit dispensing workflow?

options.A: The pharmacist reviews and verifies the order
options.B: The ward cleaner organizes the medication cart
options.C: The nurse administers the drug immediately
options.D: The patient pays the hospital cashier

explanation: Before any medication is picked or packaged, the pharmacist must check the prescription for safety and correct dosing. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h4)

question: What long-term problem can happen to the urinary tract from severe scarring due to untreated infections?

options.A: Testicular hypertrophy
options.B: Urethral strictures
options.C: Enlarged prostate gland
options.D: Chronic kidney stones

explanation: When the urethra gets badly inflamed and heals with scar tissue, it narrows down (a stricture), making it tough to pee normally.

question: A patient with severe second-degree burns across their back requires which dietary adjustment?

options.A: High protein and high calorie intake to repair damaged skin tissues.
options.B: A strict clear liquid diet to rest the gastrointestinal tract.
options.C: Zero protein to keep the kidneys from working too hard.
options.D: Low calorie intake to prevent sudden weight gain during bed rest.

explanation: Burns cause massive protein loss and high metabolic stress, requiring extra protein and calories for wound healing and tissue regeneration. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h7)

question: Why don't doctors do throat swabs for every person who walks in with a mild cold?

options.A: Most common colds are viral and resolve with supportive care
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely inaccurate for respiratory illnesses
options.C: Testing always causes severe physical trauma to the throat
options.D: Viral infections require immediate intravenous antibiotics

explanation: Exactly! Since normal colds are viral and clear up on their own, testing and antibiotics aren't needed—just rest and fluids.

question: A patient experiencing severe shortness of breath is unlikely to focus on which type of need at that moment?

options.A: Getting enough oxygen into the lungs
options.B: Achieving personal growth and self-actualization
options.C: Maintaining basic fluid balance
options.D: Relieving physical pain

explanation: Until basic physiological survival needs like breathing are met, higher-level needs such as self-actualization take a back seat. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: During which phase of the nursing process does the nurse actually perform interventions like wound care or medication administration?

options.A: Implementation
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Evaluation
options.D: Planning

explanation: Implementation is the action phase where the nurse carries out the planned care interventions. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why is using a standard checklist or form important when reviewing old patient charts?

options.A: It automatically prevents all forms of patient bias
options.B: It ensures every chart is checked for the same consistent variables
options.C: It allows the researcher to change the research question midway
options.D: It replaces the need for ethical approval from the hospital

explanation: Exactly! Using a standard form keeps your data collection neat, uniform, and organized, even when you're looking through hundreds of different patient folders.

question: Why can synergistic drug combinations sometimes lead to unexpected toxicity?

options.A: The patient's immune system attacks the combination as a foreign invader
options.B: The pills dissolve too quickly before entering the bloodstream
options.C: The drugs automatically turn into poisonous substances in the stomach
options.D: The enhanced potency applies to adverse reactions as well as therapeutic effects

explanation: Synergy is a double-edged sword! It boosts the good healing effects, but it can also accidentally ramp up nasty side effects.

question: What stimulates the kidneys to release erythropoietin (EPO)?

options.A: Elevated systemic blood pressure
options.B: High blood glucose levels
options.C: Low blood oxygen levels
options.D: Excess dietary protein intake

explanation: Hypoxia or low oxygen levels prompt renal cells to secrete EPO, which stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering furosemide to a patient with acute renal failure and fluid overload?

options.A: To permanently repair damaged glomeruli in the nephrons
options.B: To dissolve large kidney stones blocking the ureters
options.C: To lower dangerous levels of blood glucose in the body
options.D: To stimulate urine output and reduce excess body fluid

explanation: Loop diuretics like furosemide help the kidneys excrete excess water and sodium when the patient is fluid overloaded. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is the main goal of therapeutic phlebotomy in polycythaemia?

options.A: To increase blood pressure
options.B: To remove excess white blood cells
options.C: To provide iron for the liver
options.D: To reduce red blood cell mass and hematocrit

explanation: Phlebotomy is just safely removing some blood to lower the packed cell volume (hematocrit) and thin things out!

question: What is usually the very first sign of leprosy on the skin?

options.A: A discolored patch that feels numb or less sensitive
options.B: Tiny water blisters on the hands
options.C: Painful open sores on the legs
options.D: Severe itching all over the body

explanation: A pale or reddish skin patch that doesn't feel normal touch or temperature is the classic early warning sign. Keep shining!

question: What does a significantly low glucose level in the cerebrospinal fluid usually suggest?

options.A: Recent physical exercise
options.B: A normal healthy patient
options.C: A bacterial infection
options.D: Viral meningitis illness

explanation: You got it! Bacterial germs consume glucose rapidly within the spinal fluid, making the lab numbers drop below normal.

question: In public health nursing, how do we best describe a 'community'?

options.A: Any group of patients admitted to the same hospital ward
options.B: An individual family living in a single household
options.C: A group of people sharing social ties and common interests
options.D: A collection of medical doctors working in a clinic

explanation: Great job! A community is all about connection—shared ties, interactions, and a sense of belonging, rather than just being in a hospital building.

question: What is a common error that new administrators make during financial planning?

options.A: Overfunding the school clinic at the expense of classrooms
options.B: Cutting health and sanitation budgets when funds become tight
options.C: Spending all school funds exclusively on medical equipment
options.D: Refusing to accept government grants for school feeding

explanation: Exactly! Unprepared leaders sometimes treat health programs as optional extras, rather than seeing them as totally essential.

question: A patient has heavy bleeding, bad cramps, an open cervix, and reports that some tissue has passed but parts are still inside. What is this called?

options.A: Threatened abortion
options.B: Missed abortion
options.C: Incomplete abortion
options.D: Septic abortion

explanation: When some tissue comes out but part of it stays trapped inside with an open cervix, we call it an incomplete abortion. Great clinical spotting!

question: A patient vomits heavily during a cardiac arrest. What should the nurse grab right away?

options.A: The suction catheter and canister
options.B: The laryngoscope handle
options.C: The bag-valve-mask resuscitator
options.D: The endotracheal tube stylet

explanation: Well thought out! We must clear vomit immediately using suction so the airway is open and safe for breathing support. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the recommended feeding approach for a healthy infant under six months old?

options.A: Cow milk mixed with cereal in a baby bottle
options.B: Daily introduction of mashed solid family meals
options.C: Pureed vegetables combined with fruit juices
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding or infant formula feeding

explanation: For the first six months of life, breast milk or standard infant formula provides all the necessary nutrients and hydration. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the correct way to practice good cough etiquette to stop airborne germs from spreading?

options.A: Covering the face tightly with bare hands during a cough
options.B: Turning the head downward toward shared floor surfaces
options.C: Sputum expulsion directly into open waste bins
options.D: Covering the mouth and nose with a tissue or the inner elbow

explanation: Exactly! Using a tissue or coughing into your inner elbow keeps those germs off your hands so you don't pass them to door handles or other people.

question: A patient getting ready for discharge is worried about taking her pain pills right. What should you do first?

options.A: Tell the patient not to worry because pain is all in the mind
options.B: Cancel the prescription and give only herbal remedies instead
options.C: Ask a family member to manage all medication doses at home
options.D: Review the medication schedule slowly and check for understanding

explanation: Taking a little extra time to walk through the dosing schedule ensures the patient feels confident and safe at home. Excellent patient advocacy!

question: What does 'expedited partner therapy' mean in plain nursing terms?

options.A: Requiring the partner to undergo major surgery before getting drugs
options.B: Providing medication or prescriptions directly through the patient for her partner
options.C: Admitting the sexual partner into the emergency ward immediately
options.D: Sending a text message alert to all known contacts automatically

explanation: This clever strategy lets you give treatment or prescriptions straight to the patient to take to her partner, especially if he hates visiting clinics.

question: Which type of underwear helps prevent moisture buildup and lowers the risk of vulvitis?

options.A: Tight synthetic nylon shapewear
options.B: Polyester tights worn all day
options.C: Rubberized protective shorts
options.D: 100% cotton underwear

explanation: Cotton breathes easily and prevents trapped moisture, which is key because yeast and bacteria love warm, damp places. Simple prevention advice makes great nursing practice!

question: What is the main advantage of using a relative frequency column instead of just raw counts?

options.A: It shows proportions and percentages for easy comparison
options.B: It automatically changes ordinal data into interval data
options.C: It prevents outliers from appearing in the table
options.D: It corrects any typos made during data entry

explanation: Relative frequency turns raw counts into percentages, making it much easier to compare groups of different sizes. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do some families continue to practice FGM despite legal bans?

options.A: To comply with modern government health guidelines
options.B: To cure congenital abnormalities of the reproductive tract
options.C: To uphold cultural traditions, preserve chastity, and avoid social stigma
options.D: To improve the physical growth rate of adolescent girls

explanation: You got it! Deep-seated social pressure, fear of community rejection, and traditions keep the practice alive in some areas.

question: Which of the following is NOT required under standard precautions for a routine physical check?

options.A: Wearing clean gloves if contact with body fluids is expected
options.B: Cleaning stethoscope bells and diaphragms between patients
options.C: Performing proper hand hygiene before touching the patient
options.D: Wearing a full sterile surgical gown for a simple pulse check

explanation: Routine physical checks do not require sterile surgical gowns unless you are performing a sterile invasive procedure. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is a primary reason older adults have a higher risk of falling?

options.A: Higher daily fluid intake
options.B: Increased consumption of dietary protein
options.C: Slower reaction times and muscle loss
options.D: Faster bone growth in the lower limbs

explanation: As people age, natural changes like reduced muscle mass and slower reflexes make it much harder to recover balance quickly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h1)

question: Which Nigerian body is in charge of registering nurses and looking after our professional discipline?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration

explanation: Spot on! The NMCN is our very own guardian angel body set up by law to guide nursing training and practice right here in Nigeria.

question: Why are faith-based health clinics so important in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: They possess unlimited budgets from foreign governments
options.B: They charge the highest fees for specialized surgeries
options.C: They frequently establish hospitals in remote and underserved areas
options.D: They focus exclusively on urban corporate executives

explanation: Faith-based groups have a long history of setting up clinics in rural or hard-to-reach places where government hospitals might not have reached yet.

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: Providing financial aid to grieving families
options.B: Curing the underlying terminal disease completely
options.C: Speeding up the natural dying process safely
options.D: Improving the quality of life for patients and families

explanation: Think of palliative care as a comforting blanket. Its main goal is to bring peace, ease pain, and support both the patient and their loved ones through a tough time.

question: What is the main reason prolonged labour causes distress to the baby?

options.A: High levels of maternal thyroid hormones
options.B: Excessive production of amniotic fluid inside the sac
options.C: Reduced oxygen exchange across the compressed placenta
options.D: Rapid cooling of the baby's skin in the birth canal

explanation: Makes total sense! Strong, non-stop contractions squeeze the blood vessels in the placenta, meaning less oxygen gets through to the baby.

question: Why do student nurses need to know where pharmaceutical drugs come from?

options.A: To appreciate why precise dosages and chemical standardization matter
options.B: So they can manufacture the medications directly in the hospital ward
options.C: To replace traditional healers in local communities effectively
options.D: Because plant-based drugs never interact with synthetic lab drugs

explanation: Understanding drug origins helps you see why exact dosing is so vital for patient safety on the ward. Keep up the good work!

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for at the very beginning of the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Solution
options.B: Situation
options.C: Severity
options.D: Symptoms

explanation: Spot on! In SBAR, the first 'S' is for Situation—a quick summary of what is happening right now that made you call or report.

question: Why might a statistically significant result still not be enough to change everyday nursing practice?

options.A: Nurses are not legally allowed to read research papers.
options.B: P-values only tell you about sample size, not patient outcomes.
options.C: A statistically significant result may not be clinically meaningful for patients.
options.D: Statistical tests are always biased toward large hospital systems.

explanation: Spot on! Just because a number is statistically fancy doesn't mean it actually makes a noticeable, helpful difference in a real patient's life.

question: How does getting feedback from the hospital help you when you visit patients at home?

options.A: It proves to the village chief that the hospital doctors are competent
options.B: It allows the nurse to charge the patient for specialist consultation
options.C: It gives the nurse a reason to avoid seeing new clinic patients
options.D: It helps the nurse understand the final diagnosis and monitor home recovery

explanation: Spot on! Knowing the hospital's diagnosis and treatment plan lets you provide fantastic, targeted follow-up care right there in the community.

question: Your CBI patient has bright red drainage and is crying out with severe lower tummy cramps. What's the most likely issue?

options.A: Rapid healing of the surgical wound inside the bladder
options.B: A blocked catheter trapping fluid and blood clots
options.C: A normal reaction to room-temperature saline solution
options.D: An allergic reaction to the antiseptic skin wipes

explanation: Think of it like a clogged sink: fluid keeps pouring in, but nowhere to go. This stretches the bladder and causes painful cramps.

question: When the penis is resting (flaccid), what do the helical arteries do?

options.A: They pump high volumes of blood directly into the dorsal veins
options.B: They remain constricted to limit blood flow into the sinusoids
options.C: They provide somatic sensation to the skin of the penis
options.D: They actively secrete nitric oxide to maintain tissue relaxation

explanation: Well done! When resting, these arteries stay tightly clamped down so that only a small amount of blood enters.

question: What two structures combine to form the striatum?

options.A: Caudate nucleus and putamen
options.B: Putamen and globus pallidus
options.C: Caudate nucleus and substantia nigra
options.D: Thalamus and subthalamic nucleus

explanation: The caudate nucleus and the putamen together make up the striatum, which is the main receiving area for inputs coming into the basal ganglia from the cerebral cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h1)

question: A pregnant patient comes to the clinic vomiting ten times a day, unable to keep water down, and showing ketones in her urine. What condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Gestational hypertension
options.C: Normal morning sickness
options.D: Eclamptic seizure

explanation: Uncontrolled vomiting with dehydration, inability to retain fluids, and urinary ketones goes far beyond normal morning sickness into hyperemesis gravidarum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h2)

question: What is a major cause of fear for patients admitted to the hospital?

options.A: Eating meals at standard hospital times
options.B: Loss of personal autonomy and daily control
options.C: Having too many visitors during the day
options.D: Choosing their own room temperature

explanation: Spot on! Having to hand over control of your daily routine and independence to hospital staff can feel really scary and overwhelming.

question: A patient struggles to understand a complicated medication schedule with four different drugs. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to double the morning dose instead
options.B: Scold the patient for being careless with prescriptions
options.C: Stop all the medications until the patient feels better
options.D: Work with the doctor to simplify the dosing schedule

explanation: Simplifying complex regimens reduces confusion and makes it much easier for the patient to follow the treatment plan. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h7)

question: How would you best describe a skin macule?

options.A: A solid, elevated lump deep in the skin
options.B: A fluid-filled blister larger than one centimeter
options.C: A flat, unraised change in skin color
options.D: A raised, hard plateau made of merged bumps

explanation: A macule is completely flat. You can't feel it by running your finger over it—it's simply a change in color, like a freckle.

question: What is the main purpose of using the 'teach-back' method when educating patients?

options.A: Testing the nurse's ability to memorize pharmacological side effects
options.B: Allowing the patient to teach nursing students about herbal remedies
options.C: Checking whether the patient truly understands how to take their medication
options.D: Evaluating the financial cost of drugs prescribed at discharge

explanation: Well done! Instead of just asking 'do you understand?', teach-back has patients explain the instructions in their own words so you know they've got it.

question: Which of these is checked as part of a psychosocial health history?

options.A: Precise surgical incision healing progress
options.B: Coping mechanisms and daily stress management
options.C: Laboratory results from routine blood tests
options.D: Blood pressure readings taken over 24 hours

explanation: Correct! A psychosocial check looks at mental wellness, stress levels, and emotional support systems.

question: A patient with Korsakoff syndrome insists on going home to feed a pet dog that died years ago. How should you respond?

options.A: Agree that the dog is waiting at home for them
options.B: Gently redirect the patient to a current activity without arguing
options.C: Ignore the patient and leave the room immediately
options.D: Argue firmly until the patient admits the dog is dead

explanation: Arguing will only upset or confuse them. The kindest nursing move is to stay calm, validate their feelings softly, and smoothly guide them to a new activity.

question: What is the main difference between anabolism and catabolism?

options.A: Anabolism produces waste products, while catabolism produces vitamins
options.B: Anabolism occurs in the stomach, while catabolism happens in the liver
options.C: Anabolism deals only with fats, while catabolism processes water
options.D: Anabolism builds up body tissues, while catabolism breaks down molecules for energy

explanation: Well remembered! Think of anabolism as building up (like construction) and catabolism as breaking down (like demolition to release energy).

question: Which of these is completely unsafe when cleaning up a blood spill on a ward floor?

options.A: Applying a chlorine disinfectant solution over the spilled fluid
options.B: Wiping the spill immediately with a dry tissue paper barehanded
options.C: Putting on heavy-duty utility gloves before starting the cleanup
options.D: Using absorbent materials to soak up the liquid before disinfection

explanation: Never touch blood with bare hands! Always use gloves and proper disinfectants to protect yourself from infections.

question: Why do surgeons sometimes place antibiotic-impregnated beads into a bone cavity after debridement?

options.A: To act as a permanent anchor for future muscle attachments
options.B: To deliver a high concentration of medication directly to the infection site
options.C: To attract white blood cells away from the rest of the body
options.D: To permanently replace missing calcium and strengthen the bone

explanation: Antibiotic beads release local medication directly into the wound bed at high levels without causing systemic toxicity. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h8)

question: Which medication class is well-known for causing severe constipation as a side effect?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Opioid pain relievers
options.C: Short-acting diuretics
options.D: Inhaled bronchodilators

explanation: Opioids slow down the movement of the gastrointestinal tract significantly, leading to hard, difficult-to-pass stool. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T5#GNS212_U1_T5_h2)

question: How do T-cell receptors interact with epitopes differently than B-cell receptors?

options.A: T-cells bind directly to whole antigens without any assistance
options.B: T-cells require processed antigen fragments presented on cell surfaces
options.C: T-cells only recognize antigens found exclusively in fluid plasma
options.D: T-cells ignore epitopes and only target red blood cell membranes

explanation: While B-cells can spot whole antigens floating around, T-cells need other cells to chop up the antigen and show it to them first.

question: In rural Nigeria, what is a major indirect reason why mothers sometimes sadly lose their lives before reaching the hospital?

options.A: Delays in reaching a healthcare facility due to poor transport
options.B: Routine use of sterile delivery kits
options.C: Early booking for antenatal care services
options.D: Excessive consumption of local herbs

explanation: Bad roads and lack of vehicles mean transport delays are a massive hurdle. Getting mums to the clinic on time can literally save a life.

question: Why is waiting for low blood pressure a risky way to spot early internal bleeding in a young adult?

options.A: Strong compensatory mechanisms keep blood pressure normal until shock is severe
options.B: Internal bleeding actually makes blood pressure rise first
options.C: Young adults never get low blood pressure
options.D: Cuffs cannot measure pressure accurately during shock

explanation: Young bodies work overtime to hide blood loss by tightening blood vessels and racing the heart, so blood pressure can stay normal even when they're in trouble.

question: Why isn't just treating sick patients enough to stop a waterborne disease outbreak?

options.A: The environmental reservoir remains contaminated and causes reinfection
options.B: Waterborne pathogens cannot be killed by boiling
options.C: Antibiotics do not work against bacteria found in water
options.D: Patients always become asymptomatic carriers after recovery

explanation: If you don't fix the dirty water supply, people will keep drinking it and falling right back sick. You've got to fix the source!

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points towards preeclampsia in a pregnant patient?

options.A: Low blood pressure, excessive sleepiness, and hunger
options.B: Frequent urination, mild thirst, and dry skin
options.C: High blood pressure, headache, and visual disturbances
options.D: Lower back pain and increased appetite

explanation: You nailed it! Preeclampsia is marked by high blood pressure paired with stubborn headaches and blurry vision. Always watch out for this!

question: Why can taking an oral azole antifungal cause other routine medications to become toxic in the body?

options.A: Azoles inhibit liver enzymes that normally break down other drugs
options.B: Azoles force the kidneys to reabsorb all circulating prescription drugs
options.C: Azoles bind directly to other medications in the stomach and trap them
options.D: Azoles destroy the protein carriers that transport vitamins in the blood

explanation: Azoles slow down the liver's cleanup crew (P450 enzymes). With the crew on break, other drugs pile up in the blood and can become toxic.

question: Why does a midwife perform a gentle rectal exam after a delivery?

options.A: To evaluate the baseline tone of the pelvic floor muscles
options.B: To stimulate uterine contractions and prevent postpartum bleeding
options.C: To check if the anal sphincter and rectal mucosa are injured
options.D: To ensure the placenta has been completely expelled

explanation: It's a quick and necessary check to make sure a deep tear hasn't hidden itself by extending into the anal sphincter or rectal wall.

question: How does Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) differ from basic health education?

options.A: BCC focuses on active behavior change rather than just sharing information
options.B: Basic health education involves no communication at all
options.C: BCC is only used inside tertiary hospitals by doctors
options.D: Basic education is meant for children while BCC is for adults

explanation: Think of it this way: health education gives people the facts, but BCC goes a step further to help them actually overcome personal and social barriers to take action. You're building solid community nursing foundations!

question: Which of these methods is NOT reliable for destroying infectious prions?

options.A: Using disposable instruments
options.B: Extended chemical disinfection
options.C: Standard boiling in water
options.D: Specialized high-heat autoclaving

explanation: Spot on! Prions are super tough and survive normal boiling. They need heavy-duty, specialized sterilization protocols to be destroyed.

question: How does a flannel graph help you out during a community health talk?

options.A: By measuring the blood pressure of clients during community outreaches
options.B: By printing thousands of takeaway leaflets for mothers attending the clinic
options.C: By allowing the nurse to move felt illustrations on a board to tell an interactive story
options.D: By broadcasting recorded audio messages across the entire village square

explanation: Flannel graphs use fuzzy cut-outs that stick to a board. As you talk, you can move them around to build a fun, visual story with your audience!

question: What happens to a research paper if the chosen theory completely contradicts the study design?

options.A: The statistical software runs faster and processes data easier
options.B: The institutional review board grants immediate approval
options.C: The participants find it easier to complete questionnaires
options.D: The study lacks coherence and validity becomes compromised

explanation: That's right! When theory and design clash, the whole study loses its credibility and professional strength.

question: Why do pregnant women often get painful muscle cramps in their legs at night?

options.A: The heavy uterus slows down blood return from the lower limbs.
options.B: Walking too much causes permanent nerve damage in the feet.
options.C: The thyroid gland stops functioning normally during sleep.
options.D: Excess calcium builds up rapidly in the calf muscles.

explanation: The growing uterus puts a bit of pressure on blood vessels in the pelvis, which can slow down circulation and lead to those annoying calf cramps. Staying hydrated helps!

question: Which specific bacterium causes cholera?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Salmonella typhi
options.C: Vibrio cholerae
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Great recall! Cholera is caused by *Vibrio cholerae*, a bacterium that loves to hitch a ride in contaminated water and food supplies.

question: Why do doctors give epinephrine during a severe allergic reaction when airways close up?

options.A: It acts as a physiological antagonist to open airways through separate receptors
options.B: It permanently blocks the liver from making any more allergic cells
options.C: It chemically neutralizes the allergy antibodies in the bloodstream
options.D: It searches out and destroys histamine molecules directly inside the syringe

explanation: Epinephrine works through its own receptors to do the exact opposite of what the allergy is doing—relaxing the muscles and opening those airways right up!

question: When do program evaluations usually take place during a health project's lifecycle?

options.A: Every single morning during the nurse handover briefing
options.B: At specific milestones, such as midterm and project completion
options.C: Randomly without any set schedule or plan
options.D: Only after funding has completely run out and staff have left

explanation: Evaluations are scheduled check-ins at key points (like midway or at the end) to see how well the project is doing.

question: You are starting a new maternal health project in a rural village. What should be your very first step when designing its monitoring plan?

options.A: Purchase expensive computer servers for data storage
options.B: Discontinue all existing paper health registers immediately
options.C: Define the main goals and objectives of the health program
options.D: Hire international consultants to write the final evaluation report

explanation: You can't measure your progress until you clearly know what the project is trying to achieve first!

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in nursing practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing medical supplies
options.B: To ensure injections do no harm to the patient or worker
options.C: To speed up the administration of routine vaccinations
options.D: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment

explanation: Injection safety focuses entirely on protecting patients, healthcare workers, and the community from injury and disease transmission during injection procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h1)

question: How does the principle of harmony of objectives help a hospital ward?

options.A: It removes the need for performance appraisals entirely
options.B: It forces every nurse to work identical shift schedules
options.C: It ensures all nurses sing together during morning handover
options.D: It helps staff achieve personal goals while meeting hospital aims

explanation: When personal aspirations align with institutional goals, staff are happier and work harder for patient outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h2)

question: Can a person experience wellness even if they have a chronic illness?

options.A: No, chronic illnesses automatically prevent any form of social well-being
options.B: Yes, but only if they completely stop taking all prescribed medications
options.C: No, because wellness requires the total absence of any medical diagnosis
options.D: Yes, by effectively managing their condition and maintaining a positive outlook

explanation: Exactly! Having a chronic condition doesn't mean you can't live a full, happy life with proper self-care and a good mindset.

question: What delayed complication of a sting can show up days later with fever, joint pain, and a skin rash?

options.A: Hyperglycemia
options.B: Serum sickness
options.C: Cellulitis
options.D: Anaphylactic shock

explanation: Correct! Serum sickness is an immune system reaction that can pop up several days after exposure, causing fever, aching joints, and rashes.

question: What is the primary public health goal of nurse-led immunization services in primary clinics?

options.A: To provide routine nutritional supplements to infants and toddlers
options.B: To build community-wide herd immunity against preventable diseases
options.C: To completely eliminate all known chronic medical conditions
options.D: To cure active bacterial infections in hospitalized patients

explanation: Immunizations are specifically designed to protect populations by creating immunity against infectious, vaccine-preventable diseases. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h1)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand how drugs act at the cellular level?

options.A: To manufacture new pharmaceutical compounds in the ward
options.B: To bypass the need for regular patient vital sign checks
options.C: To anticipate both healing effects and unwanted side effects
options.D: To eliminate the requirement for physician prescriptions

explanation: Knowing how drugs work helps you stay one step ahead! It allows you to predict how the medicine will help your patient, and also watch out for any unexpected side effects.

question: What is the main reason a medication dropper should never touch the patient's skin or eyelashes?

options.A: To prevent contaminating the entire medication bottle with germs
options.B: To stop the liquid from flowing out too fast
options.C: To keep the glass tip from breaking off inside the canal
options.D: To avoid causing a sudden sharp pain for the patient

explanation: Touching the eye or ear transfers bacteria to the dropper tip, which then contaminates the remaining liquid inside the bottle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of epidemiological surveillance in public health?

options.A: Punishing healthcare facilities that fail to report sick patients
options.B: Providing free prescription medications to rural communities
options.C: Conducting laboratory research on new pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Continuous collection and analysis of health data to guide action

explanation: Great job! Surveillance simply means keeping a close, ongoing eye on disease numbers so health workers can spot trouble early and act fast.

question: Why do we usually avoid estrogen-containing pills for mothers who are breastfeeding?

options.A: They can significantly reduce the breast milk supply
options.B: They transfer directly into breast milk as a heavy poison
options.C: They stimulate excessive and painful uterine contractions
options.D: They always cause immediate cessation of all lochia

explanation: Estrogen can lower milk volume. That is why progestin-only options or non-hormonal methods are much safer choices for nursing mums early on.

question: Which of these is a misuse of a theoretical framework in a research project?

options.A: Aligning its core concepts with the research questions
options.B: Returning to it during the discussion section to interpret results
options.C: Mentioning it briefly in the introduction and ignoring it for the rest of the study
options.D: Using it to guide the selection of variables and measurement tools

explanation: Correct! Dropping a theory's name in the intro and never using it again leaves your study feeling disconnected and weak.

question: Where do you aim when giving a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: Deep inside the main skeletal muscle tissue
options.B: Directly into the circulating bloodstream
options.C: Into the layer of fat beneath the skin
options.D: Between the outer epidermis and the dermis

explanation: You've got this! Subcutaneous simply means 'under the skin,' targeting the fatty layer right beneath the dermis. Great job remembering your tissue layers!

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical guideline in nursing?

options.A: To punish nurses who make minor documentation errors
options.B: To help nurses make evidence-based care decisions
options.C: To increase the cost of hospital equipment purchasing
options.D: To replace doctors completely in the labor room

explanation: Guidelines provide clear, research-backed instructions so nurses know the best steps to take for specific health problems. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h2)

question: What can test scores and evaluations tell a lecturer about their own teaching?

options.A: How many hours students slept before class
options.B: Which textbooks are the cheapest to buy
options.C: How much salary the lecturer should earn
options.D: Whether their teaching method worked or needs tweaking

explanation: If a whole class misses the same question, it's a hint for the teacher to explain that topic differently. Evaluations help teachers improve too!

question: During community outreach, a nurse asks a client if they are ready to stop smoking today. Which of the '5 As' is this?

options.A: Analyze
